title: Surface tension gives the cell its outline and morphological individuality

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Surface tension gives the cell its outline and morphological individuality

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The cell is a sphere of action of localised forces, of which surface tension gives the cell its outline and individuality; partial versus total segmentation of eggs, and unicellular versus multicellular organisation, differ in whether surface tensions succeed in forming visible separations between cells.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: surface-tension is the particular force which is especially responsible for giving to the cell its outline and its morphological individuality.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “The cell as a sphere of action”. Scope: cells, segmenting eggs, Infusoria and small Turbellaria

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Force-balance models make testable shape predictions in selected systems. Public images and perturbations can assess an important role for tension, but not its sufficiency across all segmentation and organization cases.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure cortical tension, cell-boundary curvature, and separation during egg segmentation and unicellular or multicellular morphogenesis, then perturb tension and compare predicted versus observed outlines. Support requires tension changes to account for boundary formation beyond adhesion, wall, and cytoskeletal alternatives.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cell outline is jointly determined by cortex, adhesion, walls, and pressure.

The claim spans unrelated organizational scales.

Most datasets lack direct tension measurements.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Visible cell outlines are imaged in quantity, but the claim identifies surface tension as the force that creates them. That identification needs tension manipulations that are scattered and confounded with yolk and adhesion. Existing movies can test a proxy, completion of furrows, for a limited set of eggs, not the force ranking as stated for cells in general.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate the presence of visible cell boundaries in cleaving eggs to measured cortical tension, contrasting partial and total segmentation and unicellular versus multicellular organisation. Boundaries that appear only where tension succeeds, and disappear when tension is removed while adhesion is held fixed, would support the claim; boundaries set by adhesion or yolk distribution with tension unchanged would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Yolk amount and cell-cell adhesion predict partial versus total cleavage as well as tension does.

Tension during cleavage is not an archived field.

The phrase 'sphere of action of localised forces' adds no extra measurement.
